source_environment.analysis: read-only source inspection; no candidate build

observations.claim: The driver core releases devres after a failed probe without calling the driver remove callback on that failed-probe path; on normal unbind it calls driver remove first, then releases devres.

nb_fan_probe allocates the 0x58-byte chip object with devm_kmalloc and nb_fan_parse_dt allocates the 0xa8-byte subordinate state with devm_kmalloc. Those allocations are in devres; the hrtimer is embedded in the subordinate state.
observations.classification: stock call/data observation plus pinned devres contract

observations.claim: nb_fan_probe calls regulator_get and stores the returned handle at chip+0x48. The module call ledger contains no regulator_put; pinned consumer documentation says regulator_put releases the acquired regulator reference.
evidence: related_source_contracts_20261027.txt: regulator consumer docs lines 21-32 and consumer.h lines 158-170
observations.classification: unreleased-reference question; runtime leak not asserted

observations.claim: nb_fan_gpio_proc calls raw gpio_request for the speed GPIO. If IRQ conversion/registration fails, or if the later fan,pwm-gpio lookup fails after IRQ registration, the function returns an error without a gpio_free call. The module contains no gpio_free target.
The stock registers a non-devm request_threaded_irq with chip pointer as dev_id and disables it after registration. No free_irq call is present. devm_free_irq does not pair with this acquisition API.
evidence: related_source_contracts_20261027.txt: include/linux/interrupt.h declarations and kernel/irq/manage.c free_irq implementation

observations.claim: If nb_fan_gpio_proc returns an error after acquiring raw GPIO/IRQ, nb_fan_probe returns that error. If the later kobject creation or sysfs group creation fails, probe also returns an error after IRQ registration. Driver core probe-failure cleanup releases devres but does not invoke this driver remove callback.
observations.classification: static error-path relation; stale-resource consequence remains a hypothesis

observations.claim: nb_fan_parse_dt obtains child nodes with of_get_next_available_child. The pinned implementation releases prev on the next call. Label-missing, devm_fwnode_pwm_get error, and PWM apply error exits leave the loop before that next call. include/linux/of.h makes the refcount operation conditional on CONFIG_OF_DYNAMIC; the stock-target setting is not bound to this evidence. No of_node_put target appears in the module call ledger.
observations.classification: conditional OF reference-release question; target config unresolved

observations.claim: fan_speed_show starts the timer for 1 ms while holding chip mutex; the timer callback can start a further 500 ms interval and enable the IRQ. The callback later captures the count and disables the IRQ. No hrtimer_cancel or hrtimer_try_to_cancel target is present.

nb_fan_remove removes the sysfs group and clears platform drvdata, but has no observed hrtimer cancellation, IRQ release, GPIO release, regulator_put, or kobject_put. Device core releases devres after this callback returns.

The acquired kobject reference requires kobject_put when finished. sysfs_create_group failure rolls back files created by the group operation, but does not release the caller-owned kobject reference. The successful remove path removes the group but no kobject_put call is observed.
observations.classification: reference-release question on probe failure and remove

observations.claim: sysfs_remove_group/kernfs removal drains active sysfs references, but this does not cancel the independent hrtimer or release the kobject reference.
evidence: lifetime_source_contracts_MP5_20261027.txt: fs/sysfs/group.c group removal and fs/kernfs/dir.c active-reference drain excerpts

observations.claim: The mutex at chip+0x18 is initialized in probe and used in several sysfs store/show paths; the timer and IRQ callbacks update state asynchronously without using this mutex. The global chip pointer is assigned in probe and is not cleared by nb_fan_remove.
evidence: calls.jsonl mutex_lock/unlock and callback call rows
observations.classification: concurrency and pointer-lifetime relation; runtime impact unproven

observations.claim: The pinned devres core appends managed resources to the device resource list and releases the collected list in reverse order. This establishes reverse registration order (LIFO); this observation does not assert an exact order among the target driver resources without their registration sequence.

inferences: The devm-managed state, pinctrl handle, and PWM handle are released by driver-core devres cleanup; this does not automatically release raw GPIO/IRQ registrations, the regulator_get reference, the child-node reference across an early exit when CONFIG_OF_DYNAMIC is enabled, the kobject reference, or cancel the embedded hrtimer.

If a raw IRQ remains registered after an error/unbind, its dev_id points at chip state whose lifetime is controlled by devres; this creates a stale-pointer/UAF risk hypothesis, not a proven runtime failure.
sysfs_remove_group drains active sysfs operations, while an hrtimer scheduled by a completed sysfs callback may remain independently active; timer quiescence before devres release is unresolved.
unknowns: Which error predicates and DT child values occur on the actual NX809J device, and whether those paths are reached.
Whether the hrtimer can be active at each remove/unbind point under real concurrent sysfs access.
Whether the stock target is bound at runtime and which concrete PWM provider backs the dynamic apply callback.
Whether any external framework not represented in this module performs cleanup for its raw GPIO, IRQ, regulator, OF-node, or kobject acquisitions.
Whether the module-global chip pointer is ever intentionally reused or reset through an unobserved path outside the 15 stock functions.
The concurrency consequences of timer/IRQ state updates relative to sysfs mutex-protected operations.
The stock target CONFIG_OF_DYNAMIC setting is not tied to the pinned source-volume .config; the OF-child reference question remains conditional.

resource_ledger.probe_failure_release: gpio_free absent on downstream error paths
no driver remove callback after failed probe; raw registration is not devres-managed

resource_ledger.normal_release: next iteration call drops prev; full iteration reaches null call
resource_ledger.probe_failure_release: Early label/PWM errors bypass next-iteration release; explicit of_node_put absent. Refcount outcome depends on CONFIG_OF_DYNAMIC, not bound to stock target.

resource_ledger.owner: caller-owned kobject reference plus kernfs group
resource_ledger.probe_failure_release: sysfs file rollback may occur; kobject_put absent

resource_ledger.acquisition: hrtimer_init; started by fan_speed_show and callback
resource_ledger.probe_failure_release: remove not called for failed probe; timer starts only after sysfs exists, but teardown race on bound device remains

resource_ledger.users: sysfs show/store functions; timer and IRQ callbacks do not take this lock
resource_ledger.normal_release: storage released with devres after remove

resource_ledger.acquisition: assigned from devm allocation in nb_fan_probe
resource_ledger.probe_failure_release: may retain devm address after failed probe
